themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 107 this week—a 463% jump from the 19.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—signaling a sudden deterioration in road quality across Park Slope/Carroll Gardens that demands immediate investigation into root cause and extent of damage.
evidence: Street condition complaints: 107 this week vs. 19.0 weekly average (463% spike, z-score 10.79)
Concurrent spike in street sign damage: 5 complaints this week vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% increase, z-score 6.43)
Pattern suggests widespread infrastructure stress, not localized potholes
reporting_angles: What caused the sudden deterioration—winter weather, deferred maintenance, or construction activity?
Which streets are worst hit and are residents experiencing safety hazards or vehicle damage?

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals & Sanitation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped to 6 this week versus a 0.9 weekly baseline—a 586% spike with z-score 6.57—alongside an 8-complaint dumpster complaint surge 2 weeks ago, suggesting a sanitation or waste management breakdown in the district.
evidence: Dead animal complaints: 6 this week vs. 0.9 weekly average (586% increase, z-score 6.57)
Dumpster complaints: 8 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.6 weekly average (392% spike, z-score 6.43)
Convergence of two sanitation signals suggests systemic waste handling or animal control issue
reporting_angles: Are residents reporting rat problems, inadequate waste collection, or pest control failures?
Has Sanitation Department service been disrupted or are rodent populations surging post-winter?

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints hit 14 this week—a 460% surge from the 2.5 weekly average—likely reflecting winter storm aftermath, but the spike demands assessment of park safety and whether Parks Department is overwhelmed responding to emergency tree work.
evidence: Damaged tree complaints: 14 this week vs. 2.5 weekly average (460% spike, z-score 7.67)
Aligns with typical post-winter weather damage in Brooklyn
Relates to ongoing CB budget request for park reconstruction and upgrades (suggests historical underfunding)
reporting_angles: Was there a recent storm causing the tree damage spike, or is this deferred maintenance surfacing?
Is Parks Department backlogged on tree removal and posing safety risks to residents?

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from street/sidewalk activity jumped to 34 last week—a 196% increase from the 11.5 weekly baseline with z-score 6.86—suggesting construction, street fairs, or other public space activity that warrants documentation of timing and type.
evidence: Street/sidewalk noise complaints: 34 last week vs. 11.5 weekly average (196% increase, z-score 6.86)
Distinct from residential noise complaints (506 total over 90 days), indicating outdoor source
May correlate with seasonal activity or construction permits (1,050 filed in last 90 days)
reporting_angles: What street activity is driving complaints—construction, street vendors, permitted events?
Are specific blocks or intersections problem areas for late-night or early-morning noise?

themes_detail.label: Bike Infrastructure Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints surged to 4 this week (433% spike from 0.8 baseline) and bike rack complaints hit 4 (967% spike from 0.4 baseline)—small absolute numbers but extreme statistical deviation suggesting either a new micro-mobility issue or emerging bike-sharing problem in the district.
evidence: Abandoned bike complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% increase, z-score 7.51)
Bike rack complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score 7.49)
Dual spike suggests bike-sharing or cycling infrastructure problem rather than random incidents
reporting_angles: Are Citi Bike stations broken, overflowing, or malfunctioning in Park Slope?
Is there a bike theft or abandonment pattern emerging in the district?
